html:
The Battle of Lepanto was a sea battle fought on 7 October 1571 in the Gulf of Patras, off western Greece. The fleet of the Holy League, an alliance of Catholic states, destroyed the main fleet of the Ottoman Empire.

The Ottomans had invaded Cyprus, which belonged to Venice, in 1570. Pope Pius V brought Venice, Spain and smaller Italian states together to fight back. Their commander was Don John of Austria, the 24-year-old half-brother of Philip II. Each side had more than 200 galleys, warships moved by oars. The League had more guns, and six galleasses, big Venetian ships with heavy guns, which broke up the Ottoman line as it came on. Then the fleets locked together and fought hand to hand. In the centre the two flagships met, and the Ottoman admiral Ali Pasha was killed. Most of the Ottoman fleet was sunk or taken, and some 12,000 Christian galley slaves were freed.

The Ottomans rebuilt their fleet within a year and kept Cyprus. But they had lost their trained crews, and their advance in the Mediterranean slowed. Lepanto was the last great battle between galleys. Cervantes fought in it and lost the use of his left hand.
